item.title: Fallout's 2027 Return & 5 Open-World RPGs Officially Locked In
item.description:
2027 arrives in a couple of months, and plenty of games have already confirmed their plans. With its 30th anniversary coming up, Fallout should have a big year, and Bethesda has gotten the ball rolling by revealing one major release for the post-apocalyptic series. That might not be the end of things, but any other Fallout project needs to compete with a plethora of big open-world RPGs that have already staked their claim for 2027.

With the impending arrival of huge names like GTA 6 , I completely understand that some folks might see no point in looking ahead to next year. Still, it is fun to see what the future might have in store for us, especially as the 2027 calendar takes shape. What game will we be playing in 6 months? 9 months? A year?

I will only mention games/releases confirmed for 2027, even if they haven't announced specific release dates. No upcoming open-world RPGs that have yet to commit to a year.

Fallout 76's Raven Rock Acts As A Prequel To Fallout 3

A Free Expansion To Celebrate Fallout's Legacy

  • Fallout 76 expansion
  • Exact release date not confirmed
  • Bethesda's official announcement

Bethesda plans to make the most of Fallout 's 30th anniversary. Remasters of Fallout 3 and New Vegas are in the works, although 2027 releases haven't been confirmed yet. Fallout 5 is also in pre-production, but that's still a long way off from release. Bethesda will also stage a live Fallout Day Celebration in October 2027 in Washington, D.C., although we don't know much more than that for now.

So far, we do know one major 2027 release: Fallout 76 's "Raven Rock" free content expansion . The MMORPG releases significant content updates every few months for free, although they vary in scale and significance. "Raven Rock" should add a brand-new map territory, along with telling a prequel story that ties into Fallout 3 . Bethesda hasn't revealed what that might look like, but the expansion should serve as a nostalgia bridge to one of the series' most beloved entries.

New Official Fallout Release Confirmed For 2027

Fallout fans officially have a new release to look forward to in 2027.

8
By Daniel Morris

Fable Starts The Year Off With The Ultimate RPG Playground

The Most Highly Anticipated Western Open-World RPG Of 2027 (So Far)

  • Coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox Series
  • Official release date: February 23, 2027
  • Fable 's main story is expected to be around 20 hours.

Playground Games steps away from Forza Horizon to revive a beloved but mistreated RPG franchise. Xbox gamers (and, honestly, everyone) have been waiting for a new Fable for more than a decade, and it started to seem like a pipe dream; fortunately, sometimes dreams turn into reality, and a new entry is scheduled for early 2027.

Drenched in British humor and set in the most beautiful and expansive version of Albion to date, Playground's Fable looks absurdly good, although some skepticism exists due to the developer's lack of familiarity with non-racing games. Still, Playground knows how to put together an awesome sandbox, and Albion could be its masterpiece. Based on what we know, the game will prioritize reactivity over stuff like checklists and bandit camps, while still incorporating classic Fable elements like reputation, real estate, and physical changes for the protagonist.

Sagas of Lumin Lets You Fly Dragons In February 2027

Ready To Meet Your New Best Friend?

  • Coming to PC
  • Official release date: February 5, 2027
  • Semi-open world.

Fable casts a shadow over February's entire lineup, but Playground's epic isn't the month's only open-world RPG overflowing with potential. While not its only selling point, Sagas of Lumin 's dragons are its best attention-grabber, as it gives players direct control over these majestic beasts. These interactions aren't on-rail set pieces or cinematic means to fast-travel; no, you can climb, dive, hover, barrel roll, and claw your way throughout the world... also, dragons breathe fire.

When you aren't flying through the air on a sentient bringer of death, you engage in deliberately paced combat that blends weighty melee action, elemental magic, and firearms. Although only semi-open, Lumin should make for one heck of a setting, with the world being split into floating landmasses rather than just one endless terrain. That might explain why dragon riding is such a big part of the experience.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

—

More Games

Outward 2 Is 2027's Definitive Hardcore Open-World RPG

Sometimes, An Open World Shouldn't Feel Safe... Still Magical, Though

  • No confirmed release date yet.
  • Planned for PC.
  • You aren't a hero, and that's good.

Open-world RPGs come in many shapes and sizes, and Outward 2 looks to scratch an itch untouched by most other games. While survival open-world releases are relatively common, we don't really get projects that approach those concepts in the same way as Nine Dots' original Outward and its upcoming sequel.

Rather than cast you as an almighty hero destined to change the world for the better (or worse), Outward 2 sees you as an ordinary traveler just trying to survive within Aurai, a fantasy world that doesn't care if you live or die. With no hand-holding or features like a minimap, you head out on expeditions at your own risk, facing unexpected threats as they might appear. The series is known for its defeat scenarios that force you to adapt after an encounter leaves you on the verge of death, and that is merely one unique element of these games.

Initially, Outward 2 was expected to debut in 2026, but Nine Dots pushed the release back in response to player feedback on the beta.

5 Open-World RPGs With Perfect Multi-Class Systems

These open-world RPGs feature meaningful multi-classing, be it via flexible class systems, rigid hybrid builds, or consequentially bold choices.

By Christopher Adams

Final Fantasy 7: Revelation Is The Biggest Open-World RPG Of 2027 (So Far)

Finally, It Ends

  • Coming to Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PS5, and Xbox Series
  • Official release date: April 8, 2027

There's a reason I described Fable as 2027's biggest western open-world RPG , and that reason is Final Fantasy 7: Revelation . Square Enix's trilogy finally comes to an end in April, and Cloud's revamped story comes to a close with another massive open-world romp that seems set to exceed even Rebirth 's scale. The previous game didn't let you traverse the world freely until the final hours, but that shouldn't be the case with Revelation , which is aiming for "planetary scale."

Instead of relying on rigid fast-travel waypoints, players can freely pilot the vessel across the globe and skydive directly into distinct biomes, ruins, and cities below. Combat-wise, Cid Highwind and Vincent Valentine will be fully playable characters, joining a battle system expanded by a new mechanic designed around custom character builds that hearken back to FF 's old-school classes/jobs.

Look, you don't need me to sell you on FF7 Revelation ; at this point, everyone has likely decided whether they will play the final chapter or not.

Xenoblade Genesis Could Be The Best Open-World JRPG Of 2027

  • No confirmed release date yet.
  • Planned for Nintendo Switch 2.

A new console, a new era. As the franchise's first proper entry since 2022's XC3 , Xenoblade Genesis moves away from the trilogy's foundation to the point of even dropping the numbered naming convention. Anshar, the game's world, embraces high fantasy even more than its predecessors, and the Switch 2's improved power should allow for a notable jump in visual quality.

XC tends to prioritize size over fidelity, but Genesis might not need to sacrifice quite as much. Nintendo hasn't said much about Xenoblade Genesis ' story, though we know we play a character who wants to become a Vesselai, a warrior who taps into Anima, the world's power (seemingly).

item.title: World of Warcraft Forever Breaks Silence on Shared Drops and Tagging
item.description:
World of Warcraft: Forever will not include shared tagging on enemies in the open world, as Blizzard doubled down on its stance to encourage players to group up and work together when undertaking some quests. World of Warcraft: Forever is currently in a closed beta test until Wednesday, October 21.

World of Warcraft: Forever is a different take on the Classic formula compared to other versions of the long-running MMORPG. Set in an alternate Azeroth that never experienced events from subsequent expansions, WoW: Forever will allow players to uncover parts of the world that were not available in the 2004 release. This includes zones like Mount Hyjal and the magical city of Dalaran. Additionally, the Skyborne will be available as a new race for both the Alliance and the Horde factions. The game's full global release is scheduled for November 4 at 6:00 PM Eastern.

Blizzard Releases Official Statement on Diablo 5's New Plague Knight Class

Developer Blizzard issues an official comment on the first brand-new class of Diablo 5, the Plague Knight.

2
By Joshua Duckworth

World of Warcraft: Forever Holds Firm on No Shared Tagging

Although World of Warcraft: Forever has incorporated some features from Midnight , shared tagging of monsters will not be one of them. In response to a Twitter conversation between WoW content creators GingiTV and Nobbel87, Blizzard developer Josh Greenfield said that the company will "hold the line" on keeping tags and drops on a first come, first served basis in Forever . This basis is similar to other World of Warcraft: Classic modes, which Forever takes heavy inspiration from. Currently, shared tagging is available in Midnight , which prevents players from explicitly hogging a monster needed to complete an objective all to themselves. Despite the convenience, shared tagging comes at the cost of making the game a less sociable experience for players. Greenfield said that players must instead socialize and work together to overcome any friction the game throws at them.

While Blizzard admitted there are some ways it can alleviate any lingering frustrations that players may have, shared tagging is not a solution that will be implemented in World of Warcraft: Forever anytime soon. Blizzard principal game designer Johnny Cash concurred with Greenfield's statement and said that the development team will make adjustments should players encounter any issues completing a quest or objective. Given that World of Warcraft: Forever is still in beta as of this writing, some of the game's content is still subject to change pending player feedback.

Despite Blizzard's reluctance to allow shared tagging on specific monsters, World of Warcraft: Forever will include a new feature taken from Final Fantasy 14 . Drawing inspiration from Blizzard's chief competitor in the MMORPG genre, WoW: Forever beta includes an official option to play the game using a controller. Currently, 32 actions can be bound using a combination of holding the left or right trigger and pressing the D-Pad or a face button. This is similar to FF14 's Cross Hotbar (XHB) system, which has been a staple feature since the game's beginning. However, it is currently unclear if official gamepad support will extend to Midnight or other game modes.

item.title: Sega Once Tried to Cancel Sonic the Hedgehog
item.description:
Sonic the Hedgehog is one of the most beloved icons in gaming, but lead producer Takashi Iizuka says that Sega once considered ending the video game series. Starting life on the Sega Genesis in 1991, Sonic the Hedgehog quickly became the company mascot. In the decades since the original game, Sonic has starred in sequels, spin-offs, cartoons, live-action movies, comic books, and more.

The 35th anniversary of Sonic the Hedgehog is this year, and Sega has been celebrating the occasion in multiple ways. Sonic Pico Park is set to be released in November, while Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds continues to see support more than a year after its launch. The racing game failed to meet Sega's sales expectations, but the developers continue to support it through the release of free and paid content.

New LEGO Rumor is Bad News for Sonic and Animal Crossing Fans

Fans of LEGO's Sonic the Hedgehog and Animal Crossing sets could be in for bad news in 2027 if a new rumor turns out to be true.

By Marc Deschamps

Sega's Attempt to Cancel Sonic the Hedgehog

During a press pool at Tokyo Game Show, Takashi Iizuka discussed the anniversary of Sonic the Hedgehog , and some of the challenges throughout the last 35 years. Sonic has had a huge impact on gaming, but there was a point where executives at Sega apparently considered canceling the series altogether. Iizuka did not go into specific details about these discussions, but the producer claims that he had to fight to keep the series alive.

"There had been good times, and there had been bad times… during the worst times, I was told by the higher-ups that we should cancel the entire franchise. I had to fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible."

This is not the first time that Iizuka has claimed that Sega considered ending the series. Earlier this year, Iizuka said that he was specifically tasked with improving the quality of Sonic video games to keep the company from ending the series altogether. Those efforts have clearly paid off, as the last decade has seen the company put a greater emphasis on quality. Games like Sonic Mania , Sonic x Shadow Generations , and Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds have all released to positive reviews, in stark contrast to critical failures like Sonic Lost World and Sonic Boom: Rise of Lyric . As part of its efforts to improve the character's perception, Sega even delisted several underwhelming games from digital storefronts.

The Sonic the Hedgehog franchise is arguably at its strongest point ever. The Sonic movies have seen huge success at the box office, and their popularity has helped the character reach a new generation of fans. Iizuka went on to say that the first Sonic movie "definitely changed the course of this franchise." A fourth Sonic the Hedgehog movie is now in the works, and will be released in theaters on March 19, 2027. Sega even seems eager to replicate this success, as games like Streets of Rage and Crazy Taxi now have movies in development.

It's unthinkable now that Sega would have ever considered ending the Sonic franchise. The blue blur has had a huge renaissance, and it could help to drive the character's popularity for decades to come. Fans spent a lot of years disappointed by the state of the series, but things seem to be looking up. Sega has not offered details about its plans for the franchise beyond 2026. However, with a major new movie set to arrive in theaters, it's safe to imagine the next Sonic video game won't be far behind.

item.title: Pokemon TCG Collector Accused of Putting GPS on Woman's Car
item.description:
A Pokemon Trading Card Game collector pleaded no contest after he was arrested and accused of illegally placing a GPS tracker inside a delivery driver's car as a way to track card restocks. The ongoing popularity of Pokemon card releases has resulted in The Pokemon Company taking drastic measures to combat scalping and keep stocks plentiful.

The Pokemon franchise celebrated its 30th anniversary in February, which included various product releases to mark the occasion. Among these collectible releases is the Pokemon TCG: 30th Celebration expansion set, which includes reprints of cards from the game's long history, including 30 different Pikachu cards. Each reprinted card includes a special Pokemon 30th anniversary logo on the right side. 30th Celebration cards will become legal for official tournament play starting Friday, September 25, meaning TPC will continue to print the set for the foreseeable future.

Gengar Gets Brand-New Official Pokemon Design for 30th Anniversary

A Pokemon partner reveals a new design for Gengar as part of the franchise's 30th anniversary celebrations.

1
By Joshua Duckworth

Though collectors have used various methods to track when a rare Pokemon card set will be restocked, one man took it upon himself to track a delivery driver's car instead. According to Cleveland's Fox 8 News, 72-year-old Kent Kubasta of Medina, Ohio, was arrested and pleaded no contest to a charge of illegally using a GPS tracking device. Kubasta's arrest came after a woman who worked as a Walmart restock vendor said she found the GPS tracker in her car in June and notified the Wooster Police Department shortly after. The tracker was allegedly used by Kubasta to see where and when deliveries of Pokemon TCG shipments were made in the area. As part of his no-contest plea, Kubasta faces a fine of $500 and court costs, with no further penalties listed by the Wayne County Municipal Court's filing on the case.

Operation Fandom store manager Randy Kendall told Fox 8 News that Pokemon TCG collectors who want to see where card drops are occurring can instead use social media sites like Facebook and TikTok rather than rely on other methods. Kendall said that different groups can offer connections and information about card shipments to interested parties. However, the hobby of collecting and selling Pokemon cards has also been a lucrative endeavor for thieves. In August 2026, ThePokeHive in the San Antonio suburb of Castle Hills was broken into and over $100,000 in Pokemon TCG merchandise was stolen by four individuals, according to video footage.

In response to Pokemon TCG products being scalped and resold for marked-up prices, The Pokemon Company and retailers in Japan proposed a requirement to show a government-issued ID when buying Pokemon cards. This measure also extended to allowing TPC to host lotteries aimed at selling Pokemon TCG sets and cards to legitimate users. By tying a purchase to a government ID, the measures would deter accounts and bots from buying and scalping any stocks held by Japanese retailers.

However, the ongoing popularity of the Pokemon TCG 's 30th Celebration set has caused the Pokemon Center storefront to cancel orders in waves. The cancellations resulted in some customers being caught in the crossfire. With Pokemon redoubling its efforts to keep cards in stock, it remains to be seen what other measures the company can take.

item.title: Monopoly GO: Next Sticker Album Release Date
item.description:
A new sticker album gives Monopoly GO players another reason to start collecting, with fresh sticker sets, limited-time rewards, and seasonal events. The next Monopoly GO sticker album, Monster Mash, officially releases on September 23, 2026, immediately after the Happy Harvest with Looney Tunes album comes to an end. This time, Scopely is going with a Halloween-inspired theme featuring classic monsters, spooky locations, and plenty of creepy sticker sets.

Monopoly GO: Free Dice Roll Links (Updated Daily)

Players who want to get free dice rolls can do so with the Monopoly GO dice links provided in this guide.

187
By Usama Ali

Updated Sep 22, 2026, by Usama Ali: The Happy Harvest with Looney Tunes album is almost over, and Monopoly GO is getting ready for its next seasonal collection. Monster Mash brings a Halloween theme, 22 sticker sets, along with exclusive rewards and Halloween-themed collectibles. We’ve updated this guide with everything currently confirmed about the new Monopoly GO sticker album.

Next Monopoly GO Sticker Album Release Date

The Monster Mash album begins on September 23, 2026 , following the end of the Happy Harvest with Looney Tunes season. It officially starts at 1:00 PM EDT and will run until 1:00 PM EST on November 25, 2026 . This means players will have a little over two months to work through the album and collect as many stickers as possible before the season ends.

Monster Mash is clearly built around Halloween, with the sticker collection featuring spooky characters and monster-themed sets. Some of the set names include Dracula, The Swamp Monster, The Zombie, and Halloween Games.

There are 22 standard sticker sets, comprising a total of 198 stickers. The collection also includes 30 Gold Stickers, which can make completing every set more difficult. Players who finish all 22 sets will receive 15,000 Dice Rolls, the Frankie Token, and Cash.

Completing the album for the first time also unlocks the Monster Mash Prestige album, giving dedicated players more stickers to collect and rewards to win.

The Frankie Token is the main cosmetic reward for completing the regular album. Players who go on to finish the first Prestige level can also unlock the Plasma Pulse Deluxe Dice Skin.

Next Monopoly GO Sticker Album Details

The Halloween theme carries across the Monster Mash album, with the sticker sets focusing on monsters and other spooky ideas rather than the farming and cartoon theme of the previous season.

You'll inevitably end up with duplicate stickers while working through the album. Instead of simply sitting in your collection, these duplicates contribute Stars that can be exchanged through the Sticker Exchange Vault system.

If you're close to a higher Vault tier, it may be worth saving your duplicates instead of immediately exchanging them at the first available tier.

Monster Mash has three Vault tiers, with the rewards increasing as you spend more duplicate sticker Stars.

Vault Tier

As always, Scopely may change details about the upcoming album at any time, without prior notice.
